messages.content: What is the freezing point point of water at a pressure of 10 kPa?

function.name: thermodynamics_calculate_boiling_point
function.description: Calculate the boiling point of a given substance at a specific pressure. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

message.content:
At a pressure of **≈ 10 kPa** (about 0.1 atm), pure water’s solid–liquid equilibrium lies slightly above the standard 0 °C reference.  
Using the Clausius‑Clapeyron relation for the ice‑water transition (ΔHₘ ≃ 6.01 kJ mol⁻¹, ΔVₘ ≃ −9.5 cm³ mol⁻¹) gives a slope of roughly –0.003 K MPa⁻¹ for the melting line of hexagonal ice (ice Ih).  

From this:

\[
\Delta T \;=\; \frac{dT}{dP}\,\Delta P 
          \;\approx\;(-0.003\,\text{K MPa}^{-1})(-90.3\,\text{kPa})
          \;\approx\;+0.27\,\text{K}
\]

Adding this to the 0 °C reference at 101.3 kPa yields a freezing point of about **+0.27 °C** at 10 kPa.

So, under a pressure of 10 kPa, water will begin to freeze at roughly **+0.3 °C** (rounded to one decimal place).
